explanation: A central apostle who traveled around to spread Christianity, here described while working as a tentmaker in Corinth.
A Jewish teacher from Pontus who fled to Italy and later met Paul; he became an important collaborator.
Aquila's wife, who together with her husband instructed Apollos more accurately about the way of God.
A large and wealthy Greek city where Paul lived for two years and six months, founding a church there.
A companion of Paul who came from Syria to support him in his work among Jews and Greeks.
A teacher from Alexandria who was eloquent and knowledgeable about the Scriptures, but was first further guided by Priscilla and Aquila.
Proconsul (governor) of Achaia who refused to judge Paul on religious charges, thereby securing freedom for the gospel.
The trade Paulus practiced to support himself and not be a burden to the congregation he served.
